echoes.text: But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out, and leap like calves of the stall.
echoes.note: 'The sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings' — eschatological dawning healing connects to the 'light dawned' (v.16) now realized in the healing ministry. Faint, thematic.

pericopes.text: Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him. He opened his mouth and taught them, saying, “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted. Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled. Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God. Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. “Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.

echoes.text: Moses went up to God, and Yahweh called to him out of the mountain, saying, “This is what you shall tell the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:
echoes.note: Jesus 'went up onto the mountain' to teach Torah, evoking Moses ascending Sinai to receive the law; Matthew presents a new-Moses giving authoritative instruction from a mountain.

echoes.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain, and stay here, and I will give you the stone tablets with the law and the commands that I have written, that you may teach them.”
echoes.note: Moses summoned up the mountain to receive the tablets of law and commandment; the Sermon's mountain setting figurally recasts the giving of Torah.

echoes.text: Moses called to all Israel, and said to them, “Hear, Israel, the statutes and the ordinances which I speak in your ears this day, that you may learn them, and observe to do them.”
echoes.note: Moses assembles and teaches Israel the statutes; the seated Teacher addressing disciples mirrors the Mosaic instruction frame.

echoes.text: But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
echoes.note: 'The gentle/meek shall inherit the earth/land' is a near-verbatim echo of LXX Ps 36:11 (Ps 37:11), the clearest single source behind the third beatitude.

echoes.text: The Spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound; to proclaim the year of Yahweh’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all who mourn; to appoint to those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of […]
echoes.note: Isaiah's anointed proclaims good news to the poor and comfort to all who mourn; multiple beatitudes (poor, mourning-comforted, righteousness) cluster on this Servant text, which Jesus elsewhere claims.
echoes.lxxText: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach glad tidings to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind; to declare the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of recompence; to comfort all that mourn; that there should be given to them that mourn in Sion glory instead of ashes, the oil of joy to the mourners, the garment of glory for the spirit of heaviness: and […]

echoes.text: For thus says the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.
echoes.note: God dwells with the contrite and lowly in spirit; 'poor in spirit' draws on this prophetic ideal of humble dependence on God.

echoes.text: For all these things has my hand made, and so all these things came to be,” says Yahweh: “but to this man will I look, even to him who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at my word.
echoes.note: God regards the poor, contrite in spirit, who tremble at his word — background for 'blessed are the poor in spirit.'

echoes.text: Yahweh is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
echoes.note: The LORD is near the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit; coheres with poor-in-spirit and those who mourn.

echoes.text: Instead of your shame you shall have double; and instead of dishonor they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess double; everlasting joy shall be to them.
echoes.note: The mourners shall possess a double portion and everlasting joy; reinforces the inheritance/reward logic of the beatitudes.

echoes.text: Who may ascend to Yahweh’s hill? Who may stand in his holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully.
echoes.note: 'Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? ... He who has clean hands and a pure heart' — direct source for 'blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.'

echoes.text: Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
echoes.note: 'God is good to the pure in heart' — recurrent Psalter theme behind the sixth beatitude.

echoes.text: Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
echoes.note: 'Blessed is the man...' — the makarism/beatitude form itself is rooted in the Psalter's wisdom blessing formula.

echoes.text: Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man to whom Yahweh doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit.
echoes.note: Beatitude-form blessing ('Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven'); shapes the genre of Jesus' blessings.

echoes.text: They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun strike them: for he who has mercy on them will lead them, even by springs of water he will guide them.
echoes.note: The redeemed 'shall not hunger nor thirst'; background for 'hunger and thirst after righteousness ... shall be filled.'

echoes.text: Hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted in them. Then they cried to Yahweh in their trouble, and he delivered them out of their distresses, he led them also by a straight way, that they might go to a city to live in. Let them praise Yahweh for his loving kindness, for his wonderful works to the children of men! For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
echoes.note: God satisfies the hungry and thirsty soul; coheres with the fourth beatitude's promise of being filled.

echoes.text: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who has pity on the poor.
echoes.note: 'Blessed is he who is generous/merciful to the poor'; wisdom background for 'blessed are the merciful.'

echoes.text: For I desire mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
echoes.note: 'I desire mercy'; the mercy-receives-mercy logic of the fifth beatitude resonates with Hosea, a text Matthew cites twice elsewhere.

echoes.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
echoes.note: To do justice, love mercy (hesed), walk humbly — clusters mercy, righteousness, and humility that pervade the beatitudes.

echoes.text: As for me, I shall see your face in righteousness. I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with seeing your form.
echoes.note: 'I shall behold your face in righteousness' — beatific seeing of God promised to the pure in heart.

echoes.text: Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for, he said, “I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”
echoes.note: Jacob saw God face to face and lived; background to the extraordinary promise 'they shall see God.'

echoes.text: But the saints of the Most High shall receive the kingdom, and possess the kingdom forever, even forever and ever.
echoes.note: The saints of the Most High receive and possess the kingdom; underwrites 'theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven' (bracketing beatitudes 1 and 8).

echoes.text: The kingdom and the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole sky, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.
echoes.note: Kingdom and dominion given to the people of the holy ones; reinforces the kingdom-inheritance frame.

echoes.text: Didn’t you, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham your friend forever?
echoes.note: Israel as God's 'children'/friends; background for peacemakers 'called children of God.'

echoes.text: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
echoes.note: 'You are children of the living God' — divine-sonship language behind 'they shall be called children of God.'

echoes.text: Depart from evil, and do good. seek peace, and pursue it.
echoes.note: 'Seek peace and pursue it'; the active peacemaking blessed in the seventh beatitude.

echoes.text: but they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets, until the wrath of Yahweh arose against his people, until there was no remedy.
echoes.note: Israel mocked and persecuted the prophets; basis for 'so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.'

echoes.text: He said, “I have been very jealous for Yahweh, the God of Armies; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and slain your prophets with the sword. I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.”
echoes.note: Elijah laments the slaying of the prophets; the persecuted-prophets motif of v.12.

echoes.text: There was also a man who prophesied in Yahweh’s name, Uriah the son of Shemaiah of Kiriath Jearim; and he prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the words of Jeremiah: and when Jehoiakim the king, with all his mighty men, and all the princes, heard his words, the king sought to put him to death; but when Uriah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and went into Egypt: and Jehoiakim the king sent men into Egypt, Elnathan the son […]
echoes.note: The prophet Uriah killed for prophesying; concrete instance of persecuted prophets behind v.12.

echoes.text: “Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; don’t fear the reproach of men, neither be dismayed at their insults.
echoes.note: 'Fear not the reproach of men' addressed to those with God's law in their heart — close parallel to being reproached/reviled for righteousness' sake.

echoes.text: But let us lie in wait for the righteous man, Because he is of disservice to us, And is contrary to our works, And upbraids us with sins against the law, And lays to our charge sins against our discipline. He professes to have knowledge of God, And names himself servant of the Lord. He became to us a reproof of our thoughts. He is grievous to us even to behold, Because his life is unlike other men’s, And his paths are of strange fashion. We were accounted […]
echoes.note: The wicked plot against the righteous one, reproaching and persecuting him to test his patience; Second Temple background for the persecuted-righteous beatitudes.

echoes.text: Also there arose Elijah the prophet as fire, And his word burned like a torch: Who brought a famine upon them, And by his zeal made them few in number. By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven: Thrice did he thus bring down fire. How was you glorified, O Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! And who shall glory like to you? Who did raise up a dead man from death, And from the place of the dead, by the word of the Most High: Who brought down kings to […]
echoes.note: Elijah among the persecuted prophets; deuterocanonical recollection of the prophets' suffering invoked in v.12.

echoes.text: Those who sow in tears will reap in joy. He who goes out weeping, carrying seed for sowing, will certainly come again with joy, carrying his sheaves.
echoes.note: Those who sow in tears reap with joy; coheres with mourners being comforted and rejoicing.

echoes.text: Give alms from your possessions. When you give alms, don’t let your eye be envious. Don’t turn away your face from any poor man, and the face of God won’t be turned away from you.
echoes.note: Deuterocanonical exhortation to mercy/almsgiving that obtains divine favor; background to 'blessed are the merciful.'

pericopes.text: “You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men. You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden. Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house. Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

echoes.text: Every offering of your meal offering you shall season with salt; neither shall you allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking from your meal offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
echoes.note: The 'salt of the covenant' required with every grain offering; salt as covenant-fidelity image behind 'you are the salt of the earth.'

echoes.text: All the wave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer to Yahweh, have I given you, and your sons and your daughters with you, as a portion forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before Yahweh to you and to your seed with you.”
echoes.note: 'A covenant of salt forever' — salt symbolizing enduring covenant loyalty, the failure of which (losing savor) is the warning.

echoes.text: Ought you not to know that Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
echoes.note: Davidic kingship given by a 'covenant of salt'; reinforces salt's covenantal connotation.

echoes.text: yes, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
echoes.note: The Servant made 'a light to the nations/world' — direct background for 'you are the light of the world,' extending Israel's vocation to the disciples.

echoes.text: “I, Yahweh, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations;
echoes.note: The Servant given 'as a light to the nations'; reinforces the light-to-the-world commission.

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you. Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
echoes.note: Zion's light arises and nations come to its brightness; a city/light that cannot be hidden draws on this eschatological imagery.

echoes.text: It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of Yahweh’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; and all nations shall flow to it. Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.
echoes.note: The mountain of the LORD's house lifted up, with nations streaming to it; 'a city set on a hill cannot be hidden' evokes the eschatological Zion.

echoes.text: Those who are wise shall shine as the brightness of the expanse; and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars forever and ever.
echoes.note: The wise 'shall shine like the brightness of the firmament'; the radiance of the righteous behind 'let your light shine.'

echoes.text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light, that shines more and more until the perfect day.
echoes.note: The path of the righteous is like the dawning light that grows brighter; wisdom image of righteous luminance.

echoes.text: Then your light shall break out as the morning, and your healing shall spring out speedily; and your righteousness shall go before you; Yahweh’s glory shall be your rear guard.
echoes.note: When justice is done, 'your light shall break forth like the dawn'; light as visible righteous deeds (cf. 'see your good works').

echoes.text: and if you draw out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul: then your light shall rise in darkness, and your obscurity be as the noonday;
echoes.note: Doing good to the afflicted causes one's light to rise in darkness — coheres with light shining through good works.

pericopes.text: “Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill. For most certainly, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letteror one tiny pen stroke shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished. Whoever, therefore, shall break one of these least commandments, and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven. For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.

echoes.text: You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of Yahweh your God which I command you.
echoes.note: Do not add to or take from the commandment; 'not one jot or tittle shall pass' affirms the law's inviolability in the same spirit.

echoes.text: If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises in your midst you, and he gives you a sign or a wonder,
echoes.note: Warning against adding to or diminishing God's commands; background to the permanence of every least commandment.

echoes.text: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
echoes.note: 'The grass withers... but the word of our God stands forever'; heaven-and-earth-may-pass-but-the-law-endures echoes the abiding word.

echoes.text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment; and those who dwell therein shall die in the same way: but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.
echoes.note: 'The heavens shall vanish... but my salvation shall be forever' — direct background for 'until heaven and earth pass away, not one letter shall pass from the law.'

echoes.text: Yahweh, your word is settled in heaven forever.
echoes.note: 'Forever, O LORD, your word is settled in the heavens'; the eternal stability of Torah affirmed in v.18.

echoes.text: All of your words are truth. Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever.
echoes.note: 'Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever'; coheres with the permanence of the least commandments.

echoes.text: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures for ever: all those who hold it fast are appointed to life; but such as leave it shall die.
echoes.note: 'The law... endures forever' — Second Temple affirmation of Torah's eternity behind v.18.

echoes.text: From the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my ordinances, and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you,” says Yahweh of Armies. “But you say, ‘How shall we return?’
echoes.note: Call to keep and not depart from God's statutes; resonates with not breaking the least commandments.

pericopes.text: “You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not murder;’ and ‘Whoever shall murder shall be in danger of the judgment.’ But I tell you, that everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment; and whoever shall say to his brother, ‘Raca!’ shall be in danger of the council; and whoever shall say, ‘You fool!’ shall be in danger of the fire of Gehenna. “If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift. Agree with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way; lest perhaps the prosecutor deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison. Most certainly I tell you, you shall by no means get out of there, until you have paid the last penny.

echoes.text: “You shall not murder.
echoes.note: 'You shall not murder' — verbatim citation of the sixth commandment (Decalogue) introduced by the antithesis formula.

echoes.text: “You shall not murder.
echoes.note: Parallel Decalogue form of 'You shall not murder'; the cited commandment stands in both Exodus and Deuteronomy.

echoes.text: Whoever sheds man’s blood, his blood will be shed by man, for God made man in his own image.
echoes.note: Bloodshed brings judgment ('whoever sheds man's blood...'); background for 'whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.'

echoes.text: “‘Whoever kills any person, the murderer shall be slain at the mouth of witnesses; but one witness shall not testify against any person that he die. “‘Moreover you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death; but he shall surely be put to death.
echoes.note: Mosaic law on the murderer being put to death by the court; 'liable to the judgment/council' draws on this judicial framework.

echoes.text: If there arises a matter too hard for you in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, being matters of controversy within your gates; then you shall arise, and go up to the place which Yahweh your God chooses. You shall come to the priests who are Levites, and to the judge who shall be in those days. You shall inquire, and they shall give you the verdict.
echoes.note: Hard cases of bloodshed brought before judges/priests; the escalating tribunal (judgment, council) reflects Israel's courts.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You shall surely rebuke your neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
echoes.note: 'You shall not hate your brother in your heart' — the interiorizing of murder into anger toward 'your brother' draws on the Holiness Code.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: Prohibition of grudge-bearing against one's kin; coheres with reconciling before offering one's gift.

echoes.text: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell. Yahweh said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen? If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.” Cain said to Abel, his brother, “Let’s go into the field.” While they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, […]
echoes.note: Cain's anger toward his brother culminating in murder is the archetype of the anger-to-murder continuum Jesus expounds.

echoes.text: For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won’t spare in the day of vengeance. He won’t regard any ransom, neither will he rest content, though you give many gifts.
echoes.note: Wisdom on settling with one's adversary before wrath/ruin; background for 'agree with your adversary quickly... lest he hand you to the judge.'

echoes.text: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you? Debate your case with your neighbor, and don’t betray the confidence of another;
echoes.note: 'Do not hastily bring to court... settle your case with your neighbor'; coheres with vv.25-26's counsel to reconcile en route.

echoes.text: “What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?”, says Yahweh. “I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed animals. I don’t delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats. When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts? Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; new moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I can’t bear with evil assemblies. My soul hates […]
echoes.note: God rejects sacrifice from those whose hands are unjust until they do right; prophetic priority of reconciliation over cultic gift (vv.23-24).

echoes.text: I hate, I despise your feasts, and I can’t stand your solemn assemblies. Yes, though you offer me your burnt offerings and meal offerings, I will not accept them; neither will I regard the peace offerings of your fat animals. Take away from me the noise of your songs! I will not listen to the music of your harps. But let justice roll on like rivers, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
echoes.note: God despises offerings divorced from justice; background to leaving one's gift to be reconciled first.

pericopes.text: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery;’ but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart. If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna. If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.

echoes.text: “You shall not commit adultery.
echoes.note: 'You shall not commit adultery' — verbatim citation of the seventh commandment.

echoes.text: “You shall not commit adultery.
echoes.note: Parallel Decalogue form of the adultery prohibition.

echoes.text: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor’s.”
echoes.note: 'You shall not covet your neighbor's wife' — the interiorizing of adultery into lustful looking draws directly on the coveting commandment.

echoes.text: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
echoes.note: 'I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a virgin?' — the closest parallel to lustful looking already being sin.

echoes.text: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,
echoes.note: If my heart followed my eyes — the eye-heart link Jesus develops ('looks with lust... in his heart').

echoes.text: Don’t lust after her beauty in your heart, neither let her captivate you with her eyelids.
echoes.note: 'Do not desire her beauty in your heart, nor let her capture you with her eyelashes' — wisdom on lust of the eyes/heart.

echoes.text: After these things, his master’s wife set her eyes on Joseph; and she said, “Lie with me.”
echoes.note: Potiphar's wife 'cast her eyes' on Joseph; the gaze-leading-to-adultery motif.

echoes.text: Turn away your eye from a comely woman, And gaze not on another’s beauty: By the beauty of a woman many have been led astray; And herewith love is kindled as a fire.
echoes.note: 'Turn away your eyes from a shapely woman... many have been led astray by a woman's beauty' — Second Temple wisdom on the lustful gaze.

echoes.text: O Lord, Father and God of my life, Give me not a proud look, And turn away concupiscense from me. Let not greediness and chambering overtake me; And give me not over to a shameless mind.
echoes.note: Prayer against the lust of the eyes and sinful desire; coheres with guarding the eye against lust.

echoes.text: you shall not consent to him, nor listen to him; neither shall your eye pity him, neither shall you spare, neither shall you conceal him; but you shall surely kill him. Your hand shall be first on him to put him to death, and afterwards the hands of all the people.
echoes.note: Even a beloved relation must be cut off if leading to sin; background to the radical 'pluck out the eye, cut off the hand.'

pericopes.text: “It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’ but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.

echoes.text: When a man takes a wife and marries her, then it shall be, if she finds no favor in his eyes, because he has found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall write her a bill of divorce, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house.
echoes.note: 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce' — direct citation of the Mosaic divorce provision Jesus qualifies.

echoes.text: When she has departed out of his house, she may go and be another man’s wife. If the latter husband hates her, and write her a bill of divorce, and puts it in her hand, and sends her out of his house; or if the latter husband die, who took her to be his wife; her former husband, who sent her away, may not take her again to be his wife, after that she is defiled; for that is abomination before Yahweh. You shall not cause the land to sin, which Yahweh your […]
echoes.note: The fuller divorce-and-remarriage statute; Jesus reframes its concession around the cause of immorality.

echoes.text: Therefore a man will leave his father and his mother, and will join with his wife, and they will be one flesh.
echoes.note: 'The two become one flesh' — the creation order of marriage underlies Jesus' restriction of divorce (made explicit in Mt 19).

echoes.text: Yet you say, ‘Why?’ Because Yahweh has been witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion, and the wife of your covenant. Did he not make you one, although he had the residue of the Spirit? Why one? He sought a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let no one deal treacherously against the wife of his youth. For I hate divorce”, says Yahweh, the God of Israel, “and him […]
echoes.note: God hates divorce / the treacherous putting-away of a wife; prophetic background to Jesus' tightening of the divorce concession.

pericopes.text: “Again you have heard that it was said to them of old time, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’ but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God; nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black. But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not swear by my name falsely, and profane the name of your God. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'You shall not swear by my name falsely' — direct source for 'you shall not swear falsely.'

echoes.text: When a man vows a vow to Yahweh, or swears an oath to bind his soul with a bond, he shall not break his word. He shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth.
echoes.note: 'When a man vows a vow to the LORD... he shall do all that proceeds from his mouth' — basis for 'but shall perform to the Lord your vows.'

echoes.text: When you vow a vow to Yahweh your God, you shall not be slack to pay it; for Yahweh your God will surely require it of you; and it would be sin in you. But if you refrain from making a vow, it shall be no sin in you. You shall observe and do that which has gone out of your lips. Whatever you have vowed to Yahweh your God as a freewill offering, which you have promised with your mouth, you must do.
echoes.note: Vows to the LORD must be paid and not delayed; reinforces the obligation-to-perform clause Jesus cites.

echoes.text: “You shall not take the name of Yahweh your God in vain, for Yahweh will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.
echoes.note: 'You shall not take the name of the LORD in vain' — the Decalogue prohibition behind false/empty swearing.

echoes.text: He who has clean hands and a pure heart; who has not lifted up his soul to falsehood, and has not sworn deceitfully.
echoes.note: Who has not 'sworn deceitfully' — the false-oath concern of the oath antithesis (and ties to the pure in heart of v.8).

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh, “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: what kind of house will you build to me? and what place shall be my rest?
echoes.note: 'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool' — direct source for swearing 'neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God; nor by the earth, his footstool.'

echoes.text: Beautiful in elevation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the north sides, the city of the great King.
echoes.note: Zion 'the city of the great King' — direct source for 'nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.'

echoes.text: Yahweh is in his holy temple. Yahweh is on his throne in heaven. His eyes observe. His eyes examine the children of men.
echoes.note: 'The LORD's throne is in heaven'; coheres with heaven as God's throne, making oaths by it oaths by God.

echoes.text: When you vow a vow to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow. It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.
echoes.note: Better not to vow than to vow and not pay; wisdom critique of rash vows behind 'swear not at all.'

echoes.text: Accustom not your mouth to an oath; And be not accustomed to the naming of the Holy One. For as a servant that is continually scourged will not lack a bruise, So he also that swears and names God continually will not be cleansed from sin. A man of many oaths will be filled with iniquity; And the scourge will not depart from his house: If he shall offend, his sin will be upon him; And if he disregard it, he has sinned doubly; And if he has sworn in vain, […]
echoes.note: 'Do not accustom your mouth to oaths' — Second Temple wisdom counseling against habitual swearing, closely parallel to v.34.

echoes.text: Who is he who says, and it comes to pass, when the Lord doesn’t command it?

pericopes.text: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also. Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.

echoes.text: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
echoes.note: 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth' — verbatim citation of the lex talionis Jesus sets in antithesis.

echoes.text: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has injured someone, so shall it be done to him.
echoes.note: 'Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth' — parallel talion formula behind the citation.

echoes.text: Your eyes shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
echoes.note: 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth' — third Pentateuchal statement of the talion principle.

Don’t even the tax collectors do the same? If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same? Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.

echoes.text: “‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself' — direct citation of the love command, the cited half of the antithesis.

echoes.text: An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter into Yahweh’s assembly; even to the tenth generation shall no one belonging to them enter into Yahweh’s assembly forever; because they didn’t meet you with bread and with water on the way, when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you. echoes.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink:
echoes.note: 'If your enemy is hungry, give him bread' — direct wisdom command to do good to enemies, behind 'love your enemies, do good.'

echoes.text: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown;
